lesson_title: Who's On the Team? Population and the Labour Market
hook_text: Your cousin who stopped job-hunting? Officially, he's not unemployed.
clip_script: Sort one household the way the statisticians do. Gogo, seventy-two: in the population, past working age. The twins: too young. Mama at the clinic: on the team, playing — employed. Uncle S'bu, applying at three sites this month: on the team, benched but warming up — officially unemployed. Your matric sister: working-age but at school — not on the team sheet at all. And cousin Jabu — two years of applications, nothing, and this year he simply stopped asking. Here's the part that should stop you: the strict count says Jabu is NOT unemployed. He left the team sheet. The expanded count says: look at him — of course he is. That gap between the two counts? Thousands and thousands of real Jabus. And the number he vanishes into isn't the unemployment rate — it's participation, quietly falling. When you hear unemployment statistics on the news, you now know the question that matters: WHICH count — and where did the Jabus go?
visual_style: A family portrait sorting into labelled zones — population, working-age, team sheet — with S'bu glowing amber on the bench and Jabu fading off the sheet into a separate 'expanded' ledger; a national statistics board splitting into strict and expanded columns.
pacing: Person-by-person sorting rhythm, hard pause on Jabu, punchy closing question.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and read the labour statistics like an economist.
